annotations.keyFindings: Across four wards, 61 percent of admissions were screened and 34 percent of those screened were positive; only 22 percent of screen-positive patients received any intervention.
annotations.limitations: Record review; screening least complete for detained patients and short stays.

annotations.keyFindings: On one ward, nurses delivered both sessions before discharge to 38 of 52 screen-positive patients, with 81 percent of core components delivered; 24 of 41 were reached at three months.
annotations.limitations: Single ward before-after; no comparison group; telephone follow-up incomplete.

annotations.keyFindings: Fourteen trials in severe mental illness, only two with inpatients; small and inconsistent effects on drinking; high loss to follow-up; no reported harm.
Telephone follow-up three months after discharge reached 46 percent of participants; a text before the call and a second number improved response.
annotations.limitations: Two wards; response strategies changed during the study.

annotations.keyFindings: Patients found alcohol questions acceptable from the named nurse once the crisis had settled; questions on the day of admission felt accusatory.
Only 21 of 58 ward-based feasibility studies stated progression criteria in advance; studies without them described findings as promising regardless.
Mean fidelity 64 percent on psychiatric wards, falling with heavier caseloads and interruptions.

synthesis: Seven retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. Screening on psychiatric wards finds many patients with harmful drinking but rarely leads to help. One single-ward study shows nurses can deliver a two-session intervention to most screen-positive patients, while three-month telephone follow-up reaches only about half of patients. Patients accept alcohol questions from their named nurse once the crisis has settled. Trials in severe mental illness show small, inconsistent effects and rarely include inpatients, so effectiveness is not the question for this study. Feasibility studies often lack pre-stated progression criteria. The three leads suggested by the discovery reply were not retrieved and are not appraised.
gradeRationale: Single-site observational and before-after studies and small qualitative samples; consistent on delivery and follow-up difficulties, imprecise for this ward.
summary: Seven records appraised; four source-derived claims; certainty low. The unverified leads are not part of the certainty.
